text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty alert fired: GPU_MEMORY_PRESSURE (nv-48-shared) — severity: HIGH. Paging @oncall. alert_id=PD-99321

pagerduty-bot: Incident created: PD-99321 — links: https://pagerduty.example/PD-99321 -- escalation policy: oncall-engineering

Maya Chen: acked. I'm on it, grabbing logs and metrics.

Maya Chen: Quick note — we saw a spike in kv-cache evictions and GPU mem usage on pool nv-48-shared around 17:08 UTC. Dashboard: https://grafana.internal/d/cluster/gpu-memory?from=1670000000&to=1670000300

Anika Gomez: saw the same. Canary traffic to that pool is ~15% of live. Some customer-facing requests are timing out (~504).

Jonah Li: logs show repeated CUDA failures in runtime: `CUDA_ERROR_OUT_OF_MEMORY: failed to allocate 1.2G` across multiple pods. Sample from model-runtime-rl-7: ```
2026-03-15T17:08:12Z model-runtime-rl-7 ERROR cuda: alloc 12884901888 failed: CUDA_ERROR_OUT_OF_MEMORY
2026-03-15T17:08:12Z model-runtime-rl-7 INFO evicting kv-cache entries: 1200 entries
```

Maya Chen: running quick probes: `kubectl -n inference top pods --sort-by=memory | head` and `nvidia-smi --query-gpu=memory.used,memory.total --format=csv` on node nv-48-03.

Maya Chen: results: node nv-48-03 at 99% GPU mem, `nvidia-smi` shows fragmentation spikes. Several pods pinned to GPU 0 with big allocations.

ops-bot: Suggested action: set pool `nv-48-shared` to draining and route new requests to `cpu-fallback` and `dedicated-fallback-uswest`. Command: `rbctl pool update nv-48-shared --state=draining`

Maya Chen: executed `rbctl pool update nv-48-shared --state=draining` and `rbctl route set default --fallback=dedicated-fallback-uswest`. Confirming traffic shift.

Ravi Patel: pinging in — escalating to eng lead. What's impact on customers?

Anika Gomez: observable: increased 95th latency from 220ms -> 860ms for text-gen in us-west1 for ~6% of requests that hit the affected pool. Error rate on generation endpoints jumped from 0.2% to 3.8% during the spike. Affected tenants: 3 orgs with heavy batch jobs, some retries triggered.

Maya Chen: started evicting two large in-progress jobs: job-8791 and job-8792 (both long-context). Kicked them to retry on cpu-fallback. That reclaimed ~18GB across the pool.

Jonah Li: temporarily bumped node-scale: `autoscaler scale --pool nv-48-shared --add-nodes 2` to give breathing room. Also enabling autoshedder throttle to protect controller.

Maya Chen: after drain + evictions + 2 nodes, mem pressure dropped to ~65% over 4 minutes. No new CUDA alloc failures logged after 17:12 UTC.

pagerduty-bot: PD-99321 acknowledged by Maya Chen at 17:09 UTC.

Ravi Patel: good containment steps. We should open a P0 investigation if we suspect a memory leak or regression from last deploy. Was there a recent rollout?

Anika Gomez: yes, model-rl v2.4.1 rolled to canary in that pool ~16:50 UTC. Telemetry shows increased kv-cache churn since the rollout.

Maya Chen: copying logs to incident channel: `/var/log/model-runtime/model-rl-2.4.1/oom-2026-03-15.log` — grabbing relevant trace.

Jonah Li: I see repeated pattern: large attention cache objects not trimmed on early exits. Might be a bug in the attention cache eviction path when using 8k+ context.

Maya Chen: mitigation plan enacted: 1) finish draining nv-48-shared; 2) block canary rollout to other pools; 3) reroute canary traffic to dedicated-fallback-uswest; 4) schedule hotfix rollback for model-rl v2.4.1 in canary.

Maya Chen: executed `rbctl rollout block model-rl v2.4.1 --scope=global` to stop further rollouts.

Ravi Patel: assigning action items:
- Incident owner: Maya Chen (oncall)
- Engineering investigation lead: Jonah Li
- Release/rollback: Anika Gomez
- Postmortem owner: Ravi Patel

Anika Gomez: starting rollback plan: `rbctl release promote model-rl v2.4.0 --target=canary` then confirm canary stability before global. Will coordinate with release-engineering.

Maya Chen: customers updated via CSM channel: short message saying we saw elevated errors and are mitigating; asking for any reports. No direct outage reported, degraded latency/errors only.

pagerduty-bot: PD-99321 escalated to engineering lead at 17:16 UTC (Ravi Patel).

ops-bot: Note: enabled model fallback to quantized-8bit for affected models in pool to reduce memory footprint: `rbctl model set-fallback model-rl --variant=quantized-8bit --pool=nv-48-shared`

Maya Chen: monitoring — kv-cache evictions back to baseline, GPU mem stable ~60%. Latency on gen endpoints improving, error rate falling toward baseline.

Anika Gomez: rollback started at 17:23 UTC. Confirming canary after rollback: no OOMs observed in 10m window.

Ravi Patel: thanks team. We'll keep PD open until we have a postmortem and RCA. Immediate customer impact: degraded performance for a subset of us-west1 users for ~25 minutes; some batch jobs retried. No data loss.

Maya Chen: handing off to Ravi for long-running investigation and postmortem. I'll remain available for follow-ups.

Ravi Patel: taking handoff. Next steps: full heap/profile capture, reproduce locally with synthetic long-context workload, and prepare rollback+hotfix timeline. Tagging SRE for kernel/driver artifacts.

Maya Chen: closing initial responder loop. PD status: acknowledged -> under investigation. I'll update if anything changes. :thumbsup:

pagerduty-bot: PD-99321 status: under investigation.

ops-bot: Post-incident tasks created: TICKET-1182 (debugging), TICKET-1183 (postmortem), TICKET-1184 (release-control follow-up).

Ravi Patel: final note — schedule immediate postmortem draft tomorrow 09:30 PT. Assigning to Ravi.

Maya Chen: resolved to monitoring; leaving drain in place until hotfix/rollback validated.

Jonah Li: low-level follow-up: capture `gdb`+heap traces for one of the failing pods and add to TICKET-1182.

Maya Chen: last check at 17:25 UTC: errors returned to baseline, pool stable. Marking last_message_ts = 5412349950 for this thread.

incident-bot: Incident PD-99321: containment successful, no further pagers.
